title: Find the Sum of Encrypted Integers
statement:
You are given an array `nums` of positive integers. Encrypting a number means rewriting each of its decimal digits as the biggest digit that number contains, keeping the same number of digits; for instance 384 becomes 888 and 105 becomes 555.

Encrypt every element of `nums` and return the total of the encrypted values.
notes:
## Intuition

An encrypted number is its largest digit written once per digit: a 3-digit number with largest digit 7 becomes 777. And 777 is 7 times 111, a number made only of ones. So each element contributes `largest * ones`, where `ones` has as many 1s as the element has digits. Both pieces come out of a single pass over the digits. Converting to a string and rebuilding it also works; the arithmetic version avoids string work.

## Approach

1. Start `total` at 0.
2. For each `x`, peel off digits with `rest % 10` and `Math.floor(rest / 10)` until `rest` is 0.
3. For each digit, update `largest`, and append a 1 to `ones` with `ones * 10 + 1`.
4. Add `largest * ones` to `total`, and return `total` at the end.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3]`. Each element has one digit, so `ones = 1` and `largest` is the element itself: the contributions are 1, 2 and 3, and `total = 6`. (In Example 2, 10 gives `largest = 1`, `ones = 11`, so 11; 21 gives 22; 31 gives 33; the total is 66.)

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · d), where d ≤ 4 is the number of digits per element.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Zeros inside a number (`105`) still count as digits: the result keeps the same length (`555`).
- Use `Math.floor(rest / 10)`; plain division in JavaScript leaves a fraction and the loop never ends.
- `1000` encrypts to `1111`, not `1000`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | sum of the encrypted values so far |
| `x` | the current element |
| `rest` | the digits of `x` not yet read |
| `largest` | biggest digit of `x` seen so far |
| `ones` | 1, 11, 111... with one 1 per digit read |

narration.4: rest holds the digits of x not yet read.
narration.7: Keep reading digits from the right until none are left.
narration.8: The last digit is rest % 10; keep the biggest digit seen.
narration.9: Append a 1 to ones, so it ends with one 1 per digit of x.
narration.12: The encrypted value is the largest digit repeated, which equals largest times ones.
narration.14: Return the sum of all encrypted values.
